nodes.label: Clients
nodes.desc: Angular and React single-page apps. Connected clients receive state over WebSocket/STOMP instead of polling.

nodes.label: API Gateway
nodes.desc: Entry point for client requests. JWT sessions and role-based access control are enforced at the service boundary.

nodes.label: Producer
nodes.desc: A Spring Boot service that owns its domain and publishes events instead of calling downstream services directly.

nodes.label: Kafka
nodes.desc: The event backbone for high-volume transaction traffic. RabbitMQ is used alongside it where queue semantics fit.

nodes.label: Consumer
nodes.desc: Idempotent consumer: handling the same message twice has the same effect. Failures get bounded retry, then dead-lettering.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.desc: Caching layer that cuts read latency and database load.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.desc: System of record, with JPA/Hibernate tuned for fetch strategy, batch sizing and projections.

nodes.label: Dead-letter
nodes.desc: Dead-letter handling, so no message is silently lost and failed events can be inspected.

steps.text: A client sends a request through the API gateway.
The producer service validates it and publishes an event to Kafka.
An idempotent consumer picks the event up.
State is written to Redis and PostgreSQL.
The new state is pushed back to connected clients over WebSocket/STOMP.
A client request becomes an event on Kafka.
The consumer fails to process it.
It is retried a bounded number of times.
Retries exhausted: the message goes to the dead-letter queue, never silently lost.
